title: Stable Transformation of Nicotiana benthamiana
author: Jana Ordon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sbaeaie

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium tumefaciens culture
steps.instruction: Prepare the A. tumefaciens (GV3101 pMP90) strain carrying the transformation construct.

substeps.instruction: Streak strain on YEB plates containing Rifampicin, Gentamycin, and construct-specific antibiotic.
Two days prior to transformation: Inoculate 5 ml YEB liquid culture (with antibiotics) and grow for 24 h with shaking at 30 °C.
One day prior to transformation: Inoculate 100 ml induction medium (containing antibiotics) with 1 ml of the pre-culture and shake overnight at 30 °C.
Day of transformation: Pellet bacteria by centrifugation (40 ml Falcon tubes, 20 min, 4000 x g).
Resuspend bacteria in MMA medium (without antibiotics) to an OD 600 = 0.8 (50 ml).

steps.title: Sterilize Nicotiana benthamiana leaf tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest and surface-sterilize leaves from 3-5 week-old N. benthamiana plants under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Harvest 2-3 youngest, fully expanded leaves (3-5 leaves required per transformation).
Cut leaves into pieces, omitting main veins.
Incubate leaf cuts for 30 sec in 1.2 % NaOCl (+0.01 % Tween).
Wash twice in H2O (+0.01 % Tween) to remove bleach.
Store leaf cuts in H2O.

steps.title: Inoculate leaf cuts with Agrobacterium
steps.instruction: Infect the sterilized leaf tissue with the bacterial suspension.

substeps.instruction: Cut surface-sterilized leaves into smaller pieces (ca. 1x1 cm).
Pour A. tumefaciens suspension into a square petri dish.
Place leaf cuts on the surface of the suspension and incubate for at least 30 min.
Transfer leaf cuts onto a sterile piece of water-wetted Whatman paper in a fresh square petri dish.
Seal dishes with Leukopor tape and incubate for 2 days in the dark (24 °C, wrapped in aluminium foil).

steps.title: Wash and culture leaf cuts for shoot induction
steps.instruction: Remove bacteria and transfer leaf cuts to shoot induction medium.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a square dish with 50 ml H2O containing Kanamycin (100 mg/l) and Cefotaxime (250 mg/l).
Place the Whatman paper with leaf cuts upside-down onto the wash solution to release cuts; gently shake and incubate for > 3 min.
Dry leaf cuts by gently swiping on a fresh, sterile Whatman filter.
Place 8-10 dried leaf cuts per plate on shoot induction medium (MS-II) using standard round petri dishes.
Seal plates with Leukopor tape and incubate in a light cabinet (23°C, 24h light, intensity 105–125 µE m-2 s-1) for 5-6 weeks until shoots occur.
If media dry out, transfer leaf cuts/developing calli to new MS-II plates.

steps.title: Induce rooting of developed shoots
steps.instruction: Transfer shoots from MS-II to MS-III medium to induce root growth.

substeps.instruction: Cut well-developed shoots with a sterile blade as low as possible, avoiding the transfer of callus tissue.
Stick shoots (cut surface down) into MS-III medium.
Incubate under the same conditions as shoot induction (avoid red light as it prevents rooting).
Use 0.5 l Weck glasses for rooting, placing a maximum of 3 shoots per jar.
To sample independent transformants, transfer only one single shoot per callus to rooting medium.
Incubate for 2-3 weeks until roots form.

steps.title: Transfer plants to soil
steps.instruction: Acclimate rooted shoots to soil and grow to seed.

substeps.instruction: Remove MS medium from shoots/roots to avoid contamination.
Transfer shoots directly into sieved potting soil.
Maintain high humidity by placing plants in a tray covered with a lid for ~ 2 weeks.
Reduce humidity over 2-3 days by first displacing the lid and then removing it completely.
Grow plants as usual to obtain seeds.
